mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate at or below 0.25% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors shift capital toward equities amid abundant liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% in a 3-month window, it signals labor market tightness that accelerates consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP (GDPC1) over the prior 3 months indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST and GDPC1 both > 0.5% growth in 3 months) fails to predict positive returns in > 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO growth rate > 1.5% annually), manufacturing output expansion signals robust corporate capital expenditure, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods with INDPRO growth rate > 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high employment levels (PAYEMS > 140 million) indicate strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods where PAYEMS > 140 million (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it triggers central bank tightening expectations that increase equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL yoy > 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in consumer credit (RSAFS) and low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%) signal strong consumer demand and accommodative monetary policy, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS growth > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%) fails to predict positive returns in > 60% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In housing market recovery regimes (HOUST growth rate > 0.5% in 3 months), rising consumer credit (RSAFS) amplifies demand for goods and services, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods where HOUST growth rate > 0.5% in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
